question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=4x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $4\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}3{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{4})}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {e}^{u}\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{4})} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{4})}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({3}^{4}-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(81-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 80 \\  & =60\end{aligned}
$$
